labels.reasoning: Air hand: JsTs on 852r, no pair, no draw, equity 14%. Although IP and checked to, KB §1.1 says pure bluffs 3-way are unprofitable (FE ~36%) and KB DO NOT Rule #2 prohibits barreling air into 2 opponents. With better_hand_pct=0.88 and no fold equity advantage, give up and take a free card.

Air hand OOP: KhJh on A93r, no pair, no draw, 16% equity, hero is SB OOP first to act after BTN opens. KB Example 5 / DO NOT Rule #2: do not semi-bluff (let alone pure bluff) into 2 opponents OOP. Villain TP+ 11% but air 45% is split across two opponents; FE insufficient. CHECK and give up.

Drawing hand: Td9d on Jd8d3h gives flush draw + open-ender = 17 outs, equity 53% vs 27% pot odds. Not the nut flush draw and no nut blocker, so KB §1.7 RAISE conditions not met. Massive equity surplus and IP-style realization on draw — pure CALL to realize equity, BTN still behind so don't blow up the pot OOP.

River air: 9s8s on QsJd5h2c6c, missed straight draw, 0% equity. KB §1.4 3-way bluff:value ratio is ~1:4 — pure bluffs essentially eliminated on the river. Villain checked twice (some weakness signal), but with 0% equity and only ~9% worse hands, betting just gets called by everything that beats hero. CHECK.

Air with hidden equity: AdKs on Jd8d4c, draw_outs=0 in pipeline but KB Worked Example 7 covers exactly this — 6 overcard outs (~24% improvement) plus backdoor flush with Ad. Equity 24% is just under 27% pot odds, but hidden overcard equity + implied odds on TPTK improvement makes it a marginal CALL per the canonical example.

Drawing hand: Qd3d on Jd8d4c gives Q-high flush draw (9 outs), equity 38% vs 27% pot odds. Not nut flush draw → KB §1.7 RAISE conditions not met (only Q-high FD, no overcard side equity beyond Q). Strong equity surplus = pure CALL to realize draw equity, BTN still behind.

Monster: Tc9c on QhJs8d = made nut straight, equity 82%, IP, checked to. KB Worked Example 4 / DO NOT Rule #3: monsters must bet 3-way for protection — board has flush draws and one-card straight draws on future streets, two opponents drawing means slowplay risk is huge. BET 50-66% pot for value + protection.

TPGK in IP after both checked: QhJc on Q83r dry rainbow, equity 52%, villain TP+ 14% (<20% bucket = thin), villain air 51%, both checked = weakness. KB Worked Example 6 pattern (and d8886 anchor) — when villain composition is thin on value and board is dry and static, value bet small; IP makes this even stronger than Example 6's OOP version.

TPGK OOP first to act: QsJd on Q83r dry rainbow, equity 64%, worse_hand_pct 92%, villain TP+ 12% (<20% bucket), villain air 52%. This is the canonical KB Worked Example 6 spot — OOP value bet because composition shows villain compositionally thin on value and board is dry/static. The OOP penalty does not override the value extraction.

Overpair IP, both checked: JJ on 962r dry, equity 47% (overpair held back by AA/QQ/KK in CO range), villain TP+ 20%, air 51%. Dry board, IP, two checks signal weakness. Better than top pair (overpair to whole board), worse_hand_pct 93%. Bet small for value vs middle pairs and to deny overcard equity. CHECK is defensible (pot control with ~47% equity).

Overpair OOP: JJ on 962r dry, equity 61%, worse_hand_pct 94%, villain TP+ 16%, air 56%. Dry static board, JJ is near-top of hero's range here. KB Example 6 generalisation: composition is thin on value, board is static, equity well above 50% — OOP penalty insufficient. BET small for value/protection.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR MW-30: KcTh on KJ6r BB facing bet+call. KB Worked Example 3 (corrected) — pure CALL despite bet-and-call signal. Equity 44.5% vs 18.4% pot odds = 26pp surplus, villain_top_pair_plus_pct=0.31 sits in <40% bucket per §1.9 (NOT 'heavy with strong hands'), and KT dominates ~80% of continuing range. Equity surplus overrides action narrowing.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR MW-33: middle set 88 on 873r facing CO bet + BTN call. KB Worked Example 4 / Calibration Notes — monster must RAISE 3-way for value extraction and protection. Equity 90%, danger_score 0.30 (straight draws live), worse_hand_pct 100%. Pot control with a set into bet+call is value cession; raise to build the pot at compressed SPR.

Strong made AA overpair: AcAd on Js9c4d as PFA after BB checks, BTN behind. Equity 67%, worse_hand_pct 94%, villain TP+ 18%, air 44%. Compressed SPR 1.11 — checking gives BTN free card on a board with backdoor straight/flush threats. KB §1.3 says small (25-33%) c-bet sizing 3-way. BET for value and protection.

TPGK IP facing small bet (33% pot) at SPR 3.7: QcJd on Q72r dry. Equity 54% vs 25% pot odds, villain TP+ 30%, air 33%. KB Rule #5 — TP is medium 3-way, pot control. BB still behind, raising bloats the pot and gets called by better Qx. Pure CALL to keep villain's bluffs in and control pot.

TPGK IP facing 33% bet at compressed SPR 1.11: QcJd on Q72r dry, equity 56%, pot odds 27%, villain TP+ 30%. KB Rule #5 — top pair is medium-strength 3-way, BB still behind. CALL to realize equity and keep villain bluffs in; raising at SPR 1.11 commits stacks vs a range that has us in trouble when it continues.

TPGK IP deep at SPR 2.22 facing 33% bet: QcJd on Q72r dry, equity 55%, pot odds 25%, villain TP+ 30%. Same structure as MW-35/36 — KB Rule #5: TP 3-way is a pot control hand. BB still behind. CALL to realize equity and avoid bloating against a range that crushes us when it continues.

Drawing hand with §1.7 carve-out: AhJh on Kh8h3d facing BB donk 50% pot. Nut flush draw (Ah-high) + Ah blocker to villain's nut flush combos + J overcard outs + gutshot to broadway = ALL Worked Example 9 conditions met. Equity 42%, villain air 9%, TP+ 20%. RAISE per KB §1.7 — blocker raises beat fold-equity threshold even 3-way.

Drawing hand with §1.7 conditions: AhJh on Kh8h3d facing CO c-bet. Nut flush draw + Ah blocker + J overcard + gutshot — exact Worked Example 9 / MW-47 pattern. Equity 45%, BB still behind but Ah blocks villain's nut FD continuing combos. RAISE per KB §1.7 carve-out — blocker + side equity makes this +EV vs CALL.

Medium made + draw IP: QhTc on KsQd7cJh turn (2nd pair + OESD, 8 outs). Equity 30% vs 23% pot odds. KB Worked Example 8 EXACT match — multi-street aggression narrows range but 8 clean straight outs survive narrowing, IP position, pot odds nearly met. CALL is the documented action; FOLD ignores the draw equity.

Medium made + draw IP: Th8h on Ts9h4d7c turn — top pair + open-ender (J or 6 makes straight, 8 outs). Equity 35% vs 28% pot odds. Villain TP+ 67% is heavy with value, board favours BB (board_favour -0.37). But like Example 8: draw equity survives range narrowing and pot odds nearly met. CALL with the combination of pair+draw.

Drawing/air OOP: AhTc on QJ4r — gutshot to K (4 outs) + ace overcard. Equity 29%, hero is OOP first to act, no bet faced (donk option). KB DO NOT Rule #2 / Example 5 — gutshot-only with overcard 3-way OOP into 2 opponents is check/fold territory; do not donk-bluff. CHECK and proceed cheaply.

Strong made TPTK turn IP, both checked at compressed SPR 0.47: AdKd on As9c5dTc, equity 54%, worse_hand_pct 75%, villain TP+ 40% (≥40 bucket = meaningful value density). Turn brought T (gutshot complete on board now), checking gives free card to draws. KB Rule #5/Example 4 logic — at SPR 0.47 with TPTK and turn drawing texture, BET for value and to charge straight draws.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR MW-50: JcTc on J845 turn after CO bet, BTN raise flop, BB call, BTN bets again. KB DO NOT Rule #3 + Calibration Notes — flop check-raise/raise into 2 opponents 3-way is near-nuts; villain TP+ 72%, board_favour -0.43, equity 0%. Top pair weak kicker dominated by raised+bet range; range fold.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR d8886: QcJc on 2s5dJd — top pair good kicker, equity 60%, villain TP+ 18% (<20% thin), air 59%. Compressed SPR 1.25 BB OOP. Per Calibration Notes pass condition: BET (or difficulty 3 with BET as primary alternative). KB Example 6 generalisation — composition thin on value, hero TPGK at top of own range, value bet for protection on diamond draw board.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR d2410: JcKs on Jd9d3h6d turn, villain checked back flop. TPGK with K-kicker, equity 45%, villain TP+ 33%, air 20%, checked-back signals weakness. Per anchor: BET. KB §1.10.4 nut_made_block reasoning — hero's Jc removes JJ trips combos; villain's checked-back range is weaker than composition suggests. BET for value at compressed SPR.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR d8963: JhJc on Ks4h9c3h turn, villain checked back. JJ underpair to K, equity 39%, villain TP+ 28%, air 1% (low). Solver 50/50 mixed per Calibration Notes; pass = BET. Checked-back signals weakness; JJ has good showdown but at SPR 1.25 with two hearts on turn, BET small to deny equity to overcard floats and turn flush draws. CHECK is defensible.

CALIBRATION ANCHOR d3178: AcAs on JhQcJcKs5h river, checked to. AA overpair on 4-card broadway+paired board, equity 60%. Per anchor: BET. Compressed SPR 1.25 — at this stack depth, AA is a pure value bet against villain's checked range that contains plenty of worse Qx, Kx, and Jx busted draws.

Strong made but dominated: 7h6h on Qd8d6sQh turn = two pair (Qs and 6s on paired board). Equity only 27.5% — every Qx counterfeits hero (Q-high two pair beats 6s+Q). villain TP+ 56%, villain checked back flop. KB Rule #5 and pot control — two pair where hero is dominated by every Qx is a CHECK. Turning hand into bluff makes no sense; take showdown route.

Medium made TP weak kicker BB OOP: 8cKc on KdTd4s, equity 54%, villain TP+ 20% (<20% thin), air 34%. Two-tone diamond board, compressed SPR 1.25. KB Rule #5 says TP is medium 3-way (lean pot control) — but with composition thin on value, donk/lead small (25-33%) for protection vs flush draws and to deny equity to overcards. CHECK is defensible. Difficulty 2-3.

Medium made TP weak kicker CO OOP, villain checked back flop: 3sKs on 7d9h5sKc turn — top pair turned, equity 54%, villain TP+ 27%, air 28%, checked-back = weakness. Static board (no flush, marginal straight). Similar to d2410 pattern: when villain shows weakness and hero turns top pair, BET for thin value and to deny equity. CHECK is defensible at low SPR for showdown.

Medium made TP weak kicker OOP on wet board: 6dKd on KhQc9d. Equity 47%, danger_score 0.30 (straight + flush draws live), villain TP+ 28%, air 24%. Connected two-tone board favours BTN's range (suited connectors smash KQ9). KB Rule #5 — TP weak kicker on dynamic board OOP is a pot control hand; betting gets raised by better Kx and folds out air. CHECK to realize equity.

Monster: 5h5d on 5s6d6h = fives full of sixes. Equity 90.5%, worse_hand_pct 99.6%, monster=1. KB Worked Example 4 / DO NOT Rule #3 — monsters must bet 3-way. Villain air 72% means lots of folding range, but value extraction from any 6x and overpairs is the priority. BET for value; pot control a near-nuts hand on a paired board is value cession.
